alex: FYI perf runs after the recent runtime tweak show a regression on the KV prefetch path — ~12% tail latency bump on our seq=2048 E2E bench.

alex: nsys timeline snapshot (trimmed):
```
GPU memcpy HtoD  68ms  (spike at t=1.2s)
kernel: select_kernel_v2  4ms per call  (invocations doubled)
kernel: kv_prefetch_loop  90ms total  (hotspot)
CPU spin on lock_wait  120ms
```

meera: which runtime change? kernel-selector rewrite from last week? commit range?

alex: last good was ab12c3d, first bad ef45g6h — change landed in ab12c3d..ef45g6h (kernel-mux refactor + heuristic tweak)

diego: can you paste the exact repro command you used? I want to re-run locally with nsys.

alex: repro: `./bench/run_end2end.sh --model=tiny --seq=2048 --batch=4 --requests=1000`
nsys command I ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=run_4282 ./bench/run_end2end.sh ...`
I attached the .qdrep to the workspace (perf link in thread).

sam: Saw same on Dedicated qtr-2 cluster — eviction_count for KV cache jumped ~3x during the run. Logs: `kv_evictions=312 -> 987` after the change. Also noticed more frequent kernel re-selection at warmup.

meera: sounds like selector is issuing more frequent warmup probes which thrash KV cache. Could be heuristic boundary for sequence length. Any perfetto timeline showing KV cache hits vs evictions?

alex: perfetto trace: https://internal.perfetto/trace/4282 (short summary in the qdrep). The timeline shows repeated `kv_load` -> miss -> `memcpy` -> load fallback pattern.

diego: quick theory: new mux prefers a smaller-block kernel for some mid-length sequences, causing extra memcopies to/from staging buffers. We should bisect to identify the exact commit.

meera: agree. Proposed bisect steps: 
1) git checkout ab12c3d
2) run `./bench/repro_nsys.sh` (script captures qdrep + nvtx)
3) git bisect start ef45g6h ab12c3d
4) bisect run `./bench/repro_nsys.sh`

alex: doing an initial bisect pass now. leaving a note: the bad runs show `selector_choice=kernel_A (fallback)` while good runs pick `kernel_B` consistently.

sam: I can reproduce locally if you need. If we confirm kernel_A is the culprit, I can roll an emergency revert for the heuristic only (keep mux change).

diego: before revert, can we add lightweight logging in the selector to dump `(seq_len, batch, chosen_kernel, estimated_bytes)` for 1k requests? patch snippet: 
```cpp
// selector debug dump
if (FLAGS_selector_debug) 
  LOG(INFO) << seq_len << " " << batch << " -> " << chosen.name() << " (" << est_bytes << ")";
```

meera: that should help correlate memcopy spikes with choices. Also add a metric for `kv_eviction_rate` to the bench harness.

infra-bot: deploy_pipeline: Triggered perf job on `staging` with commit ef45g6h (job id job-9853).

alex: bisect update: first failing commit pinned to ef2b9c0 (heuristic tweak in selector weighting). I'll paste the nsys diff after I finish the run.

alex: nsys diff (before vs after trimmed):
```
BEFORE: selector -> kernel_B (no staging memcpy)
AFTER:  selector -> kernel_A (staging memcpy x2 per token loop)
Memcopy time increased +48ms on average across hot trace window
KV cache misses +2.7x overall
```

meera: ok that's pretty conclusive. Two actionable options: revert the heuristic change, or adjust kernel_A path to avoid extra staging memcpy (probably better long-term).

diego: I'll prototype avoiding staging memcpy by reusing pinned buffer when possible. If we go revert route, let's do a targeted revert of the weighting change only (safe path).

sam: +1 for targeted revert for immediate mitigation. I'll prepare an RFC for changing kernel_A implementation to eliminate the extra copy.

alex: created PR for targeted revert -> PR #4216. Also pushed debug selector logging to branch `selector-debug-4282` with sample logs uploaded.

meera: great. once PR merges, let's rerun the bench and confirm: target <3% tail delta and kv_evictions back to baseline.

diego: noted. I'll continue on the memcpy-free kernel_A experiment and post perf comparisons next update.

sam: thanks all — ping me if you need a revert roll-forward in production. :thumbsup:
